Lewy body

glossary.Umbrella term: A general name covering several related conditions.
glossary.Intellect: The ability to think, reason and understand.
glossary.Early-onset: Starting at a younger age than usual, here before 65.
glossary.TIAs: Transient ischaemic attacks: brief stroke-like episodes that resolve within 24 hours.
glossary.Focal neurological signs: Signs pointing to damage in one area of the nervous system, such as one-sided weakness.
glossary.Parkinson's disease dementia: Dementia developing in someone who has had Parkinson's disease for over a year.
glossary.Interlocking pentagons: Two overlapping five-sided shapes the patient copies to test visuospatial skills.
glossary.Compulsivity: Repeating behaviours driven by an urge that is hard to resist.
glossary.Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis: The commonest motor neurone disease, causing progressive muscle weakness.
glossary.Visual hallucinations: Seeing things that are not there.
glossary.Autonomic dysfunction: Failure of the automatic nervous system controlling blood pressure, gut and bladder.
glossary.Antipsychotics: Dopamine-blocking drugs such as haloperidol, used for psychosis and agitation.
glossary.Psychomotor slowing: Slowed thinking and movement, typical of severe depression.
glossary.Self-neglect: Failing to look after one's own hygiene, food or health.
glossary.10-CS: The 10-point cognitive screener, a brief memory and orientation test.
glossary.6-item screener: A brief six-question test of recall and orientation.
glossary.MIS: Memory Impairment Screen, a short test of delayed recall.
glossary.Mini-Cog: A quick screen combining three-word recall with a clock-drawing test.
glossary.TYM: Test Your Memory, a self-completed cognitive test.
glossary.FBC: Full blood count: haemoglobin, white cells and platelets.
glossary.U&Es: Urea and electrolytes: kidney function and salts.
glossary.INR: A clotting test measuring how long blood takes to clot.
glossary.Haematinics: B12, folate and iron studies, checked because deficiencies can cause reversible cognitive decline.
glossary.TFTs: Thyroid function tests, since hypothyroidism can mimic dementia.
glossary.Bone profile: Blood calcium, phosphate and alkaline phosphatase.
glossary.Reversible causes: Treatable problems that mimic dementia, such as low B12, hypothyroidism or depression.
glossary.Cortical atrophy: Shrinking of the outer grey matter of the brain.
glossary.Infarcts: Areas of tissue death caused by loss of blood supply.
glossary.Frontotemporal atrophy: Shrinking of the frontal and temporal lobes, seen in FTD.
glossary.Lumbar puncture: A needle into the lower back to sample or drain cerebrospinal fluid.
glossary.Ventriculoperitoneal shunt: A tube draining excess brain fluid from a ventricle into the abdomen.
glossary.Prolonged QT: A lengthened QT interval on ECG, raising the risk of dangerous arrhythmias.
glossary.Heart block: A delay or failure of electrical conduction from the atria to the ventricles.
glossary.Sinus bradycardia: A normal heart rhythm with a rate under 60 beats per minute.
glossary.Cholinergic: Relating to acetylcholine; cholinergic side effects come from too much of it.
glossary.Bradycardia: A heart rate under 60 beats per minute.
glossary.Glutamate: The main excitatory neurotransmitter; too much damages neurones.
glossary.Bio-psycho-social: Looking at biological, psychological and social factors together.
glossary.Psychoeducation: Teaching patients and carers about the illness and how to cope.
glossary.Advance care planning: Discussing and recording future care wishes while the person can still decide.
glossary.Amitriptyline: A tricyclic antidepressant with anticholinergic effects that worsen cognition.
glossary.Memory clinic: A specialist service for assessing and treating memory problems.
glossary.SSRIs: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, antidepressants such as sertraline.
glossary.Plaques: Clumps of protein outside nerve cells, here made of amyloid-beta.
glossary.Hyperphosphorylated: Carrying too many phosphate groups, which makes tau clump into tangles.
glossary.Synaptic loss: Loss of connections between nerve cells.
glossary.Multi-infarct disease: Many small strokes adding up to cognitive decline.
glossary.Small vessel disease: Damage to the brain's tiny arteries, causing scattered white matter injury.
glossary.Posterior cortex: The back part of the brain's outer layer, including parietal and occipital lobes.
